best_for: Experienced Windows users who want to decide app by app what may reach the network, and who are fine starting from block-everything.
description:
simplewall is a small network filtering tool for Windows, written by the developer who goes by Henry++. The program is less than a megabyte, and its README is blunt about the audience: it is meant for advanced users.

You can write global rules that apply to every app, or special rules for the apps you pick, using IP addresses, ranges, CIDR blocks and ports. When you switch filtering on, choose permanent rules or temporary ones that reset at the next reboot. It can notify you about dropped packets and log them to a file, and it covers Microsoft Store apps, Windows services, WSL and IPv6. The command line can turn filtering on or off without the window, and the binaries come with a GPG signature you can check.

points.title: Blocks everything first
points.text: Out of the box every program is blocked, and you allow the ones you trust. The upside is quiet control over what phones home; the cost is a short period of fixing apps that suddenly lose their connection.

points.title: Not a Windows Firewall skin
points.text: It writes rules straight into the Windows Filtering Platform and does not touch Windows Firewall. You can leave Windows Firewall on; the two run side by side.

points.title: Rules stay after you close it
points.text: Filters keep working when the app is closed, and uninstalling does not remove them. Press "Disable filters" before you uninstall, or connections may stay blocked.

points.title: Built-in telemetry blocklist
points.text: An internal list blocks known Windows telemetry hosts. You can switch it off under Settings, Blocklist, if it breaks something you use.

points.title: Expect a few side effects
points.text: Windows may show a network icon with an exclamation mark, and Windows Update may need an allow rule. The README explains both fixes. There is no Windows Security Center integration.

points.title: Free, GPL-3.0, admin needed
points.text: It costs nothing and the code is open. It needs administrator rights and Windows 7 SP1 or later on 64-bit or Arm64. Dropping a `simplewall.ini` file in its folder makes it portable.

points.title: 26 versions, one installer type
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 26 versions. Each is a machine-wide x64 installer; the project offers no macOS or Linux build.
